candidate.blueprint_topic: Health-promotion counseling for metabolic risk reduction
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with MASLD that individualized weight management, healthy dietary patterns, regular physical activity, and control of metabolic risk factors are foundational lifestyle interventions across the disease spectrum.

options.A: Use an individualized plan that supports healthy weight management, regular aerobic or resistance activity, and a nutrient-dense dietary pattern while addressing metabolic risk factors.
options.B: Eliminate all dietary fat because total fat avoidance is the primary evidence-based treatment for MASLD.
options.C: Lifestyle changes are useful only after advanced fibrosis has developed and offer little value earlier in the disease course.
options.D: Physical activity has no meaningful role in MASLD management if liver enzymes remain abnormal.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current AASLD guidance uses the updated term metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and continues to emphasize lifestyle intervention as a core component of management. Weight reduction when appropriate, healthy dietary patterns, and regular physical activity can improve hepatic steatosis and cardiometabolic health and should be individualized to the client's needs and abilities. B is incorrect because current guidance does not recommend eliminating all dietary fat; dietary quality and overall energy balance are more relevant than a blanket fat prohibition. C is incorrect because lifestyle intervention is relevant before advanced fibrosis and is used to reduce metabolic and liver-disease risk across the MASLD spectrum. D is incorrect because exercise has independent metabolic and hepatic benefits and is not dismissed solely because aminotransferases are abnormal. The final item replaces outdated NAFLD terminology with current MASLD nomenclature and avoids unnecessary numeric weight-loss thresholds in the tested answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current AASLD sources directly support MASLD as the current nomenclature and identify weight management, healthy diet and regular physical activity as foundational lifestyle interventions.
